headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 6 studies yielded an effect size of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.72–1.29), indicating no statistically significant association between tea and bladder cancer. Although the point estimate suggests a potential inverse relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 88.52%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
